questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following compound.

The compound undergoes reaction with two equivalents of diisobutyl aluminium hydride followed by acid hydrolysis to provide P as the major product. The structure of P is:
questions.solution:
The given compound contains an ester group ($-\text{CO}_2\text{Et}$), a nitrile group ($-\text{CN}$), and an isolated carbon-carbon double bond.

Diisobutylaluminium hydride (DIBAL-H) is a selective reducing agent. When 2 equivalents of DIBAL-H are used followed by acid hydrolysis:
1. One equivalent reduces the ester group to an aldehyde ($-\text{CHO}$).
2. The second equivalent reduces the nitrile group to an imine intermediate, which upon acid hydrolysis yields an aldehyde ($-\text{CHO}$).
3. DIBAL-H does not reduce isolated $C=C$ double bonds.

Therefore, both the $-\text{CO}_2\text{Et}$ and $-\text{CN}$ groups are converted to $-\text{CHO}$ groups, while the cyclohexene ring remains intact. This corresponds to the structure given in option (A).

Answer:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Halogenation of ketones is an interesting reaction. For example, it is involved in the preparation of haloforms. Halogenation using molecular halogen takes place at the $\alpha$ position to the carbonyl group in the presence of an acid or a base. In a basic medium, the stability of carbanion is important. In an acidic medium stability of enol form is important, as the reaction goes through enol.


An $\alpha$-halogenated ketone undergoes subsequent halogenation to form polyhalogenated ketone. Chloroform is prepared by the action of sodium hypochlorite on acetone. In this process trichloroacetone is formed as an intermediate. Trichloroacetone can react with hydroxide ion in two possible ways as shown below.
(i) $\mathrm{CCl}_3 \mathrm{COCH}_3+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{HO}^{-}} \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH}+\mathrm{CHCl}_3$
(ii) $\mathrm{CCl}_3 \mathrm{COCH}_3+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{HO}^{-}} \mathrm{CCl}_3 \mathrm{COOH}+\mathrm{CH}_4$
The correct statement(s) is/are:
options: Reaction of 2-bromo-3-pentanone with bromine in an alkaline medium would give mainly 2,4-dibromo-3-pentanone.
Methyl ethyl ketone reacts with chlorine in the presence of an acid to form 3-chloro-2-butanone.
In an alkaline medium, reaction (i) is favoured over reaction (ii) due to stabilization of carbanion.
